change_summary: oya-http-middleware-kernel: HyperRequest/HyperResponse renamed to HttpRequest/HttpResponse; body type Bytes→Vec<u8>; bytes dep removed. Hyper adapter does Vec<u8>↔Bytes conversion at the boundary. Three middleware crates + ops-workspace-shell-runtime updated to consume new types and drop bytes. Root-cause seam fix.
schema_v2_backfill_note: v2.0.0 added F8_performance + F9_compliance as required facets. This evidence file was authored against v1.0.0 (7 facets). Back-filled F8 + F9 below per the v1→v2 migration policy.

mechanical_proof.cargo_test_summary: cargo test: 102 passed (10 suites, 0.03s) across oya-http-middleware-kernel, oya-http-runtime-hyper-adapter, oya-http-{deadline,telemetry,tenant}-middleware-domain, oya-http-sse-kernel, oya-ops-workspace-shell-runtime, oya-foundry-adapter-{anthropic,openai}-compat-api. Plus 10 additional tests in adapter (incl. boundary_conversion_round_trip_identity tokio::test asserting byte-equality on 256-byte payload).
mechanical_proof.seam_audit_before: 6 Cargo.toml files declared hyper-family deps (kernel + 3 middleware + adapter + ops-runtime); 5 .rs files imported hyper/bytes/hyper_util/http_body_util.
mechanical_proof.seam_audit_after: 1 Cargo.toml (oya-http-runtime-hyper-adapter) declares hyper-family deps; 1 .rs file imports them. Reproducible via: `for d in crates/*/Cargo.toml; do if grep -E "^(hyper|hyper-util|http-body-util|bytes)( |\.workspace|\s*=)" "$d" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "$d"; fi; done`

findings: Eliminated the type-misnomer special case: kernel types named after a concrete provider (Hyper*) in a transport-neutral kernel was a self-contradiction.

Eliminated the bytes-in-kernel double-bookkeeping leak: previously the kernel declared bytes::Bytes in its public body field, forcing every consumer to also pull bytes. Now the kernel uses Vec<u8>; conversion happens once, at the adapter boundary.
Deleted no fields, no enum variants: Linus would approve — the data structures stay essential; only the body-type choice changed.

Conversion cost: Vec<u8>→Bytes is zero-copy via Bytes::from(Vec<u8>) (Bytes adopts the buffer). Bytes→Vec<u8> via .to_vec() is one allocation. The latter happens once per request on the inbound boundary; bounded by the request body size limit Phase 8 will install.
Cargo build graph shrinks for 5 crates: they no longer pull bytes transitively (kernel + 3 middleware + ops-runtime).
No duplication of cargo-audit / cargo-deny logic; the seam-check lane (Phase 11) will integrate them, not reauthor.
fixuptasks: F-PERF-BODY-COPY-1: if request body is >1 MiB AND not yet bounded by Phase 8 policy, the Bytes→Vec<u8> copy on inbound becomes a perf concern. Re-evaluate when load test shows it.

F3_adversarial.failing_fixture_id: INTERNAL: corrupting the Bytes::from() call (e.g., Bytes::from_static(b"x") instead of Bytes::from(resp.body)) is REJECTED at compile-time by type-check + at test-time by the round-trip assertion which iterates all 256 byte values.
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: panic: 'Vec<u8> -> Bytes -> Full -> collect -> Bytes must be byte-identical' with byte-position diff
F3_adversarial.self_critique_fixup_applied: First version of this test only asserted status==200, not byte equality. Caught during F5 self-review; fixed before claiming complete. Real fix: tokio::test draining Full<Bytes>.collect().to_bytes() and asserting byte-equality + length + first+last byte sentinels. Iterative-fix-loop applied per /specs/iterative-fix-loop.json.
findings: All 102 tests pass including new construction-without-bytes tests (http_request_buildable_with_std_only, http_response_buildable_with_std_only, not_found_carries_canonical_body, method_not_allowed_carries_canonical_body, with_body_accepts_vec_from_string).

Telemetry middleware ships an EXPLICIT bug-documenting test (known_bug_capture_value_appearing_elsewhere_is_overrewritten) that asserts the S6 leak class exists. Phase 4 (F-MULTI-Q1) replaces this with a positive assertion that the bug is GONE.
Type names now match doc-comments. A reader of oya-http-middleware-kernel no longer has to mentally translate 'why is this called Hyper if it's transport-neutral?'
Body literal pattern: contributors write `b"hello".to_vec()` instead of `Bytes::from_static(b"hello")`. Same length, no new dep cost.
Adapter consumers (closure handlers) write Vec<u8> bodies; no Bytes import needed.

Self-caught quality issue mid-Phase: my own adversarial test for boundary_conversion_round_trip_identity was originally a stub that only asserted status. Name lied about coverage. Fixed by making it async (tokio::test) and draining the body via http_body_util::BodyExt::collect to assert byte-equality on full u8 range.

Documented quality issues NOT fixed this phase (existing, named, deferred): telemetry hot-lock (F-MULTI-Q2), deadline fake enforcement (F-MULTI-Q3), restrictive SyncHandler signature (F-MULTI-Q4), tenant-id grammar in middleware (F-MULTI-Q5). Each will be fixed in its own Phase (4-7) with its own adversarial fixture.
fixuptasks: F-MULTI-Q2: telemetry sharded counters — Phase 5 (deferred to FixupTask, not Phase 2)

alternatives_named: Option A — IP-002 as written (rename crates + strip bytes from middleware only): rejected. Cosmetic; left the kernel still using Bytes; would require per-consumer manual cleanup whenever a new crate is added.

Option α — generic HttpRequest<B = Vec<u8>>: parametric over body type. More expressive but propagates trait bounds through the entire middleware chain + handler signatures. Rejected for this phase as over-engineering before we know we need it.
Option γ — HttpBody enum {Vec(Vec<u8>), Streamed(...)}: rejected as speculative; no streaming consumer today, would freeze a design before requirements known.
Option β — concrete Vec<u8>: SELECTED. Minimal API surface, std-only, zero-copy at the Bytes::from boundary, drop-in compatible with all existing middleware via straightforward Vec literals.
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Vec<u8> hits the F2-hyperscaler test (scales linearly with body size, bounded by Phase 8 limits) AND the F4-ergonomic test (new contributors don't learn a new body type) AND the F1-linus test (no special-case state machine for body kinds). When streaming routes arrive, introduce a separate Streamed variant or HttpStreamRequest type — not a premature enum.
rejected_reasons: γ (enum body): speculative; design freeze before requirements.

findings: Vec<u8> body type chosen over Bytes for simplicity (Option β). This introduces one allocation + one copy on every inbound POST/PUT body — measurable at >5k req/s with body sizes >4 KiB.
Outbound Vec<u8> → Bytes is zero-copy via Bytes::from(Vec<u8>) which adopts the buffer.
No benchmark added this phase; perf is intuition-grade not measurement-grade.
fixuptasks: F-PERF-BODY-COPY-1 (re-evaluate when load test shows >1 MiB legitimate bodies on hot routes)

findings: Type rename + body parameterization touches no tenant-scoped or regulated data class. HttpRequest/HttpResponse carry INTERNAL_ONLY data_class markers (preserved through the rename).

findings.summary: S3 — adapter still reads full request body into memory without a per-route or global limit. Attacker sends 10GB → adapter OOMs. Existing pre-Phase-2 issue, NOT introduced by this phase but EXPLICITLY left as Phase 8 work.
findings.recommended_action: Phase 8 installs MaxBodyBytes policy + http_body_util::Limited at adapter intake.

findings.summary: S4 — no connection/idle timeouts on hyper-util builder. Slowloris feasible. Existing pre-Phase-2 issue.

Internal: Bytes::from(Vec<u8>) zero-copy semantics confirmed by Rust docs but not by the hyper crate's stability contract. If a future hyper version changes this, performance regresses silently (correctness preserved).
findings.recommended_action: Pin hyper version in Cargo.toml workspace deps (already done per ADR-0090); flag in dependency-rationales overlay.

decision_log_row: Phase 2 (kernel rename + body parameterization) is the load-bearing architectural change of this multi-day session. Eliminated 5 special cases (one type misnomer, one kernel dep leak, three transitive consumer leaks).
